narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **27% chance** you may not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that your school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—your current path has some risks, and these courses are a way to give you the support you need to stay on track.

The biggest factor pushing this prediction is your **alcohol consumption during the week**. Most students in your school drink very little or not at all on weekdays, but your reported consumption is much higher. Heavy drinking on school days can make it harder to focus, stay motivated, or keep up with assignments—all of which directly affect your grades. This is the strongest signal the model picked up, and it’s a clear area where small changes could make a big difference.

Another important piece is your **history of past failures**. Unlike most students who haven’t struggled before, you’ve had some setbacks in earlier classes. While this alone doesn’t guarantee failure, it suggests you may need extra help to build confidence and catch up on foundational skills. The model also noticed that your **parents’ education level** is lower than average for students who pass without extra support. This doesn’t mean your family’s background is the reason you’re at risk, but it does highlight that having fewer academic resources at home can make schoolwork feel more challenging.

The good news? These courses aren’t a punishment—they’re a chance to address the things holding you back. Focus on cutting back on alcohol during the week, use any extra support available to you, and make the most of the remedial classes. Small, consistent efforts in these areas can help you turn this prediction around.
